items.title: Decision Report - RZ05/24, 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol, (Aypa Power)
notes: Report from Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services outlined the scope of the proposal, the related planning policies and the processes undertaken to date. She indicated after reviewing the application, all the information and studies provided, and comments received, it is staff’s opinion the planning policies of the PPS have been met and any concerns raised can be addressed during the site plan process and secured through legal agreements. Staff is recommending Council approve the zoning amendment application and endorse the County OPA. She noted if approved, the by-law would be brought forward to Council for enactment after the County OPA is adopted, as required by the Planning Act.

Staff and a representative from Aypa Power responded to questions regarding the extent of the landscaping proposed, the purpose of the fire tank, maintenance to be addressed through site plan approval, and potential impact to insurance costs.

Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development clarified Council’s role in the site plan approval process, indicating changes to The Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13 requires the appointment of municipal staff to approve site plans.
Dan Wilson, CAO provided details on the purpose of the community benefits agreement which is separate from the planning approval process.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 7:20pm.

items.title: Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan - Preliminary Preferred
notes: Alternative
Report from Ryan Maiden, Water and Wastewater Capital Project Manager

Adam Gilmore, Manager of Engineering and Ryan Maiden, Water and Wastewater Capital Project Manager and John Tyrrell, RV Anderson and Associates provided the overall approach, indicating the Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan will identify capacity constraints and identify and evaluate opportunities to increase system capacity to accommodate for growth to the 2051 planning horizon. They provided an overview of the 2051 wastewater requirements, the current site constraints and provided two options: 1) Retain Fergus WWTP as a Conventional Activated Sludge (CAS) facility and expand capacity via a new 3rd Liquid Train; or 2) Convert Fergus WWTP to a Membrane Bio- Reactor (MBR) facility.

John Tyrrell outlined the two options, noting Option 1 is the preferred option and he outlined the next steps in the process. He responded to questions regarding the reliability of the technology, the roll out of an Annual Storm Drainage Disconnection Grant Program, funding opportunities, and no expansion beyond OPA126.

items.title: New Township Operations Centre Update - Guaranteed Maximum Price
notes: Contract Award

Report from Brandon Buehler, Operations Centre Project Manager Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services, Brandon Buehler, Operations Centre Project Manager and Adam Gilmore, Manager of Engineering provided an update on; a) the progress, including the works completed to date, b) the sustainability and green building features incorporated into the design, c) the grant funding opportunities, on the potential solar panel options under consideration and d) to present the guaranteed maximum price and overall construction budget.

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer indicated the financial strategy to fund to project is structured around growth components being funded through development charge serviced debt, and non-growth components being serviced through reserve funds and the proceeds of land sales.

Staff responded to questions regarding the potential impact of Bill 17, the fluctuating real estate market, projects management costs, green house capacity and future needs, debt financing and zero impact to taxation.

items.title: Paid Parking Program
notes: Report from Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, including community and stakeholder engagement conducted and the overall plan for paid parking. He indicated the recommended paid parking program will include two distinct parking zones:
Zone 1 – paid parking with high turnover (3hour time limit) Zone 2 – paid parking for longer-term parking (current by-law up to 24 hours)

D. Wilton responded to questions regarding the need for additional accessibility parking and additional 15 minute and loading and unloading zones, parking permits, need for clear signage, success of the downtown shuttle and the upfront costs – renting vs purchase.

motions.item_title: New Township Operations Centre Update - Guaranteed Maximum Price
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves the Guaranteed Maximum Price and Overall Construction Budget for the new Operations Centre as outlined in Report IS2025-15, and authorizes staff to reach agreement with the Design-Builder (Ball Construction Ltd.) on the Guaranteed Maximum Price in the form of a change order to the existing Design-Build Contract; AND THAT Council directs staff to proceed with construction of the new Township Operations Centre with substantial completion anticipated by December 2026; AND THAT Council directs staff to further investigate solar power generation opportunities for the site and report back to Council with a recommended option and financial analysis; AND THAT Council directs staff to submit an application for grant funding through the Municipal Fleet Electrification Grant Fund offered by the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) to fund the cost of proposed EV charging stations and electrification of the Township's existing vehicle fleet; AND THAT Council receives for information the staff recommendations regarding potential amendments to the capital forecast with respect to this project. AND THAT Council direct staff to investigate a total debt issue of $33.9 million dollars, to be drawn as needed to satisfy the debt supported capital needs for the 2025 and 2026 calendar years, and return to Council with the necessary financing, debt policy, and any associated by-laws once established.

AND THAT Council direct staff to investigate a total debt issue of $33.9 million dollars, to be drawn as needed to satisfy the debt supported capital needs for the 2025 and 2026 calendar years, and return to Council with the necessary financing, debt policy, and any associated by-laws once established.
